mainTopic: Splitting the robber's payment and אשם between priestly shifts, the order of payment before אשם, and why the חומש does not hold back atonement
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: a woman is content with any marriage, as ריש לקיש's saying shows. Then the גמרא turns to a robber (גזלן) who gave his payment and his אשם to two different priestly shifts, יהויריב and ידעיה. רבא explains that both items were given during יהויריב's week. רבי יהודה fines ידעיה for taking money out of turn, so the money joins the אשם. The רבנן fine יהויריב for taking the אשם before the money, so the אשם joins the money. Several ברייתות of רבי then apply רבי יהודה's view to special cases. In one, the first אשם was already offered and יהויריב keeps its hide. In others, one shift or both let their week end without asking for the item. רבא then shows from the words 'with which he will atone' that the money must come before the אשם. Finally, a ברייתא about מעילה, together with a two-way comparison to גזל הגר, teaches that the ram and the קרן are both required for atonement but the חומש is not. With that, the פרק הגוזל עצים ends.

steps.title: A woman is content with any marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an answer from the previous discussion: a woman is happy with any kind of marriage, as ריש לקיש's saying shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is satisfied with any arrangement at all, like ריש לקיש said: 'Better to sit as two than to sit alone like a widow.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes an answer that began on the previous page. It says a woman is satisfied with any marriage arrangement, and it supports this with a saying quoted by ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a woman would still have agreed to the marriage even if she had known about a possible later difficulty. Being married at all is worth more to her than being alone. ריש לקיש's saying gives that attitude in a short folk phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: it is pleasing / acceptable to her
with anything at all
two bodies, meaning as a married pair
widowhood, being alone

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the earlier topic. It has nothing to do with the robbery case that starts right after it.

phrases.english: that it is satisfactory for her with any arrangement at all
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer from the previous page. 'Her' is the woman being discussed there.

phrases.english: in line with Reish Lakish, as Reish Lakish said:
It is better to sit as two bodies
phrases.notes: In other words, it is better to be married.

phrases.english: than to sit as a widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous page.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman would accept marriage under any terms, so her original consent still stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Being married at all is preferred over being alone, as ריש לקיש's saying shows.

steps.title: Dispute over returning the money or the guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about giving the money to יהויריב, then brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about the reverse case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה: 'He gave the money to יהויריב...' Our רבנן taught: if he gave the אשם to יהויריב and the money to ידעיה, the money goes back to join the אשם, says רבי יהודה. The חכמים say the אשם goes back to join the money.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes our משנה about a robber who must pay back money and bring an אשם. It then brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about what happens when the two items went to two different priestly shifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is that the אשם went to the יהויריב shift and the money went to the ידעיה shift. רבי יהודה says the money must move over to יהויריב, so the shift holding the אשם gets both. The חכמים say the opposite: the אשם must move over to ידעיה, so the shift holding the money gets both.

keyTerms.meaning: guilt offering the robber must bring
name of one priestly shift
name of the next priestly shift
he must return / it must be moved back
our Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)

phrases.english: 'He gave the money to Joiarib,' etc.
Our Rabbis taught:
If he gave the guilt offering to Joiarib
and the money to Jedaiah,
the money must be returned to be with the guilt offering,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
the guilt offering must be returned to be with the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the money moves to the shift holding the אשם. חכמים: the אשם moves to the shift holding the money.

steps.title: What case is the dispute about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. If each shift received its item during its own week, both should simply keep what they got.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he gave the אשם to יהויריב during יהויריב's week and the money to ידעיה during ידעיה's week, then each one acquired what is rightfully its own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to picture the case of the ברייתא. It shows that the most obvious picture does not work, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each shift received its item during its own week, both acted properly. Then there would be no reason to take anything away from either one. So the ברייתא must be talking about a different situation.

keyTerms.meaning: what are the circumstances?
if you say
its shift, its assigned week
acquired what belongs to it

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that he gave the guilt offering to Joiarib
during Joiarib's watch,
and the money to Jedaiah during Jedaiah's watch,
then this one acquired what is its own
and that one acquired what is its own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case of the ברייתא from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case would anything be taken away from either shift?
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each shift received during its own week, both acquired properly, so nothing should be returned.

steps.title: רבא: both were given during יהויריב's week
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that both the אשם and the money were given during יהויריב's week, so ידעיה took the money outside its own week.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: we are dealing with a case where he gave the אשם to יהויריב during יהויריב's week, and the money to ידעיה, also during יהויריב's week.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by setting up the exact case. Both items were handed over during יהויריב's week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only thing that changes from the rejected picture is when the money was given. It was given to ידעיה during יהויריב's week, which was not ידעיה's turn. Because of this, each side can find something improper, and the argument is about whom to fine.

keyTerms.meaning: with what are we dealing here?
the אמורא who gives the answer

phrases.english: Rava said:
With what are we dealing here?
where he gave the guilt offering to Joiarib
during Joiarib's watch,
and the money to Jedaiah
also during Joiarib's watch.
phrases.notes: This is the key change: ידעיה took the money during a week that wasn't its turn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by defining the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both items were given during יהויריב's week, so ידעיה received the money out of turn.

steps.title: רבי יהודה fines ידעיה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says ידעיה is fined because it took money when it was not its week, so the money goes to יהויריב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: since it was not ידעיה's week, we fine ידעיה. Therefore the money goes back to join the אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now explains רבי יהודה's reason. ידעיה did wrong by taking the money outside its week, so ידעיה loses it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the problem is ידעיה acting when it was not its turn. The fine falls on ידעיה. The money moves to יהויריב, which already holds the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: we penalize / fine
since
therefore

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
since it is not Jedaiah's watch,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: we penalize Jedaiah;
therefore the money is returned to be with the guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יהודה's side within רבא's case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ידעיה is fined for receiving out of turn.

steps.title: The רבנן fine יהויריב
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say יהויריב did wrong by accepting the אשם before the money was paid, so יהויריב is fined and the אשם goes to ידעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: the members of יהויריב acted improperly when they accepted the אשם before the money. Therefore we fine them, and the אשם goes back to join the money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the רבנן's reason. They focus on a different mistake: יהויריב accepted the אשם too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money must be paid before the אשם is accepted. יהויריב took the אשם first, so for the רבנן they are the ones at fault. The fine falls on them, and the אשם moves to ידעיה, which holds the money.

keyTerms.meaning: not according to the law, improperly
before
them themselves

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree there is a fine. They only argue about who did wrong. רבי יהודה says ידעיה, for taking money outside its week. The רבנן say יהויריב, for taking the אשם before the money was paid. Whichever shift is fined loses its item to the other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a fine (קנס) can decide which priestly shift ends up with both the payment and the offering.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
the members of Joiarib acted improperly
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: in that they accepted the guilt offering before the money,
therefore we penalize them,
and the guilt offering is returned to be with the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the same case explained in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהויריב is fined for accepting the אשם before the money was paid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת is about which shift to fine: ידעיה for acting out of turn, or יהויריב for taking the אשם first.

steps.title: If יהויריב already offered the אשם, a new אשם is brought
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that according to רבי יהודה, if יהויריב offered the אשם first, the גזלן brings a second אשם for ידעיה to offer, and each shift keeps what it has.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי said: According to רבי יהודה, if the members of יהויריב went ahead and offered the אשם, the person brings another אשם. The members of ידעיה offer it, and each group keeps what is already in its hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא in which רבי works out what happens under רבי יהודה's view if יהויריב already offered the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the money should go to יהויריב. But here יהויריב offered the אשם before the money was paid, so that אשם did not count. A new אשם is needed, and since ידעיה is holding the money, ידעיה offers the new one.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
רבי יהודה הנשיא, who wrote down the משנה
They went first, acting before they should have
Another guilt-offering
They acquired it and get to keep it

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
if the members of Yehoyariv went ahead
and offered the guilt-offering,
he must go back and bring another guilt-offering,
and the members of Yedaya will offer it,
and these acquired what is in their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יהודה's ruling from step 5 to a case where יהויריב already offered the אשם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יהודה's view, if יהויריב offered the אשם early, a second אשם is brought and offered by ידעיה, and each shift keeps what it holds.

steps.title: What could יהויריב possibly keep from an invalid אשם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what use the first אשם is to יהויריב, since it is a פסול offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: They ask: What is it good for? It is a disqualified guilt-offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the end of the ברייתא, which says יהויריב keeps what it has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first אשם was offered before the money was returned, so it is פסול. If it is invalid, it seems there is nothing for יהויריב to gain from it, so the words "they acquired what is in their hands" look empty.

keyTerms.meaning: They say, introducing a question
What is it fit for?
Disqualified, invalid

phrases.english: They say: What is it good for?
It is a disqualified guilt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the final phrase of step 7, "וזכו הללו במה שבידן".
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that יהויריב keeps what is in its hands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An invalid אשם seems to give the כהנים nothing, so there is nothing for them to acquire.

steps.title: רבא: יהויריב keeps the hide
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that what יהויריב keeps is the hide of the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is talking about its hide.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by explaining what יהויריב actually gains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the אשם was invalid, its hide still has value. That hide is what "they acquired what is in their hands" refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Its hide (the animal's skin)

phrases.english: Rava said: For its hide.
phrases.notes: The members of יהויריב keep the skin of that first animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the ברייתא means: the gain is the hide, not the offering itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An invalid אשם gives the כהנים nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהויריב acquires the hide of the first אשם.
steps.whatToRemember: Even an invalid אשם leaves something of value, its hide, and that is what יהויריב keeps.

steps.title: If the אשם still exists, it goes to the money
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא of רבי: according to רבי יהודה, if the אשם has not yet been offered, it goes to the money, meaning to ידעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי said: According to רבי יהודה, if the אשם still exists, the אשם should be sent back to where the money is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא of רבי about the case where יהויריב has not yet offered the אשם. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ruling is that the אשם goes to the shift holding the money, which is ידעיה. That seems to be the reverse of what רבי יהודה said earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Still exists, not yet offered
He should return or send back
To, next to, where something is

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi said:
According to the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
if the guilt-offering still exists,
he should return the guilt-offering to the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא about the case where the אשם was not yet offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יהודה's view, an אשם that still exists is sent to the shift holding the money.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה said the money goes to the אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבי יהודה holds the money is returned to the אשם, not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהודה holds that the money should be returned to the אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between this ברייתא and רבי יהודה's known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהודה ruled that ידעיה is fined and the money goes to יהויריב, which holds the אשם. Now רבי says in רבי יהודה's name that the אשם goes to ידעיה, which holds the money. These two rulings point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, introducing a challenge
He holds this view

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: יַחֲזִיר כֶּסֶף אֵצֶל אָשָׁם אִית לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: holds "return the money to the guilt-offering"!
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's ruling from earlier, that the money goes to יהויריב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10 using רבי יהודה's ruling from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's statement that, according to רבי יהודה, the אשם goes to the money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה ruled the opposite: the money goes to the אשם.

steps.title: The case is where יהויריב's shift ended without asking for the money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא speaks of a case where יהויריב's week ended and they never demanded the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where the shift of יהויריב ended and they did not demand the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by limiting the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally רבי יהודה says the money goes to יהויריב. But here יהויריב finished its week without claiming the money from ידעיה. That changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
His shift, the week of priestly service
They demanded it

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
For example, where the shift of Yehoyariv ended,
and they did not demand it.
phrases.notes: "It" means the money that ידעיה was holding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's ruling contradicts רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling applies only where יהויריב let its shift end without claiming the money.

steps.title: יהויריב gave up its claim to the money
steps.stepSummary: The lesson of the ברייתא is that by not demanding the money, יהויריב waived it in favor of ידעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this teaches us that they gave up their claim in favor of the other shift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the lesson behind רבי's ruling and wraps up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Staying quiet until the shift ended counts as giving up the money. Once ידעיה rightfully keeps the money, the אשם goes to them as well, so there is no contradiction with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us
They waived or gave up their right

phrases.english: And this teaches us
that they waived it in their favor.
phrases.notes: יהויריב gave up the money to ידעיה by never asking for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 12 by stating its lesson.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Not claiming the money before the shift ends counts as giving it up, so the money stays with ידעיה and the אשם goes to them.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה normally sends the money to יהויריב. If יהויריב let its week end without asking for it, they gave it up, and the אשם follows the money to ידעיה.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי יהודה changed his opinion. His basic rule stays the same. Only in this special case, where יהויריב gave up the money, does the outcome flip.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: the money goes back with the אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that according to רבי יהודה, if the אשם is still around, the money returns to be with the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא says: רבי said, according to רבי יהודה, if the אשם has not yet been offered, the money goes back to be with the אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא. In it, רבי explains how רבי יהודה rules when the אשם has not been offered yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money and the אשם are supposed to stay together with the same משמר. Here רבי says the money follows the אשם, so it goes back to the משמר that holds the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא teaches
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה
Still around, not yet offered
The guilt-offering brought by the thief

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא,
Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: Plain "רבי" means רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is a different person from the רבי יהודה in the next line.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
if the guilt-offering is still in existence,
the money returns to be with the guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא of רבי on the same topic, after the first one was explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, if the אשם still exists, the money goes back to it.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי needs to tell us this, since it is רבי יהודה's known opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! That is exactly what רבי יהודה holds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It looks like it is only repeating what we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that רבי יהודה says the money goes back to the אשם. So a ברייתא that only repeats this seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to find the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
He holds this opinion

phrases.english: It is obvious!
This is what he holds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא just quoted for teaching nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי in step 14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It only repeats רבי יהודה's known opinion, so it seems pointless.

steps.title: The case: both watches ended and nobody asked
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where the weeks of both משמרות ended and neither one demanded anything from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? A case where the shift of both groups ended, and they did not ask each other for anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by giving the ברייתא a special case. Both משמרות finished their week and stayed quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself is known. The new point is how it applies when neither group demanded the money or the animal from the other. The next step explains why this case is worth teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Their משמר, the group of כהנים serving that week
They demanded

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Such as where the watch ended
of these and of those,
and they did not demand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא only repeats רבי יהודה's basic rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: It speaks about a case where both משמרות ended without any demand.

steps.title: Silence is not giving up: go back to the basic rule
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought both sides gave up their claims. The ברייתא teaches that we go back to the original rule instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said they each gave up their claim to the other. So it teaches us that since they did not demand, we go back to the first rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the new point of the ברייתא. Not asking does not count as giving up, so the money goes back with the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'might have thought' is that silence means each group waived its claim in favor of the other. The ברייתא rejects this and returns to the basic setup: the money joins the אשם. This differs from the earlier ברייתא (step 13), where only one side stayed silent and that silence did count as waiving.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
They gave up their right, waived
It teaches us
At the start, the original situation

steps.whatToRemember: When both משמרות end their week without demanding anything, we do not assume they gave up. The money goes back to be with the אשם.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 13. There, one side's silence meant it gave up the money. Here both sides were silent, so we go back to the basic rule.

phrases.english: Lest you say
they waived in favor of each other,
it teaches us that we say:
since they did not demand,
let them return to the beginning.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the money comes before the אשם?

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the rule about the order. It is setting up a search for the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says you are only יוצא if you return the stolen money first and then bring the אשם. The גמרא asks which פסוק teaches this order.

keyTerms.meaning: His stolen item
Et cetera; the rest of the משנה
From where do we know these things?

steps.title: רבא: the word 'besides' shows the money comes first

steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק, 'האשם המושב' means the stolen money that is given back. The ram is described as something 'besides' the money. רבא reads this as showing that the money is already there before the ram is brought.

steps.title: Challenge: does 'besides' always mean 'after'?
steps.stepSummary: One of the חכמים points to 'besides the morning עולה' in the מוספין and asks whether the מוספין then come first too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the חכמים said to רבא: if so, the פסוק says 'besides the morning עולה.' Should we also learn from this that the מוספין come first?
steps.whatsHappening: A חכם challenges רבא's way of reading the word 'besides'. He uses another פסוק to show where this reading leads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'besides X' means X comes second, then the פסוק about the מוספין would mean they come before the morning תמיד. The questioner treats this as a result that cannot be right, so רבא's proof looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, according to your logic

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the way רבא read the word 'מלבד' in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of 'מלבד' as showing order
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading of 'besides the morning עולה' would put the מוספין before the תמיד, which is treated as impossible.

steps.title: Nothing may come before the morning תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The challenger supports his question with a ברייתא: nothing may be offered before the morning תמיד. So 'besides' cannot mean that the other thing comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: how do we know nothing may come before the morning תמיד? The פסוק says 'and he shall arrange the עולה on it', and רבא explained: 'the עולה' means the first עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from step 20. It brings a ברייתא showing that the morning תמיד must come before everything, including the מוספין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word 'besides' meant 'the other thing comes first', then 'besides the morning עולה' would make the מוספין come before the תמיד. But the ברייתא, as רבא himself explains it, says the תמיד is always first. So the word 'besides' cannot be what teaches order, and רבא's source in step 19 seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא (opens a challenge)
The daily morning offering
The פסוק says (introduces the source)

steps.confusionAlert: Note the twist: the רבא who learns 'the first עולה' here is the same רבא being challenged. His own explanation is being used against his reading of 'besides'.

steps.title: רבא learns the order from 'with which he will atone'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that his source is not the word 'besides'. It is the future-tense phrase 'with which he will atone', which shows the אשם comes after the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I learn it from 'with which he will atone'. When he is paying, he has not yet atoned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by pointing to a different phrase in the same פסוק as his real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With which he will atone' is in the future tense. At the time the money is returned, the ram has not yet atoned, so the אשם must come later. This avoids the problem with 'besides', so the מוספין question no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: With which he will atone (future tense)
It is learned from (literally, it comes out for him)

steps.title: If he brings only the payment or only the אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's next line about giving the קרן, and quotes a ברייתא about מעילה. The ברייתא asks how we know that bringing only one of the two, the payment or the אשם, is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He gave him the קרן, etc.' The רבנן taught: how do we know that if he brought his מעילה payment but not his אשם, or his אשם but not his מעילה payment, he has not fulfilled his obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic from the משנה and sets up a ברייתא's question. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about someone who used הקדש property, who must repay it and also bring an אשם. It asks for the source that both parts are required, in either order of what is missing. This sets up the discussion of what does and does not hold back atonement.

steps.title: Both the ram and the payment are needed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק 'with the ram of the אשם, and he will be forgiven'. Forgiveness comes only once both parts are brought.

steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'the ram' as the offering and 'האשם' as the payment. Since 'and he will be forgiven' comes only after both are mentioned, missing either one means he is not yet forgiven.

steps.title: What if the offering came before the payment?

steps.title: The payment must already have been made
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'with the ram of the אשם'. This means the 'אשם' (the payment) was already given before the ram is offered.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word 'אשם' means the payment (the קרן), not the animal. The ram is offered 'with' an אשם that is already there. So the payment must be made before the offering, and an offering brought too early does not count.

steps.title: Does the extra fifth also hold back atonement?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that perhaps the חומש is also required for atonement, just like the ram and the payment.

steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram and the קרן are both required, and missing either one blocks atonement. The person also owes a חומש, so one might think it works the same way. The word 'יכול' signals a first guess that the ברייתא will reject.

steps.title: Only the ram and the payment are required
steps.stepSummary: The verse mentions only the ram and the אשם before 'and he will be forgiven'. So in הקדש only those two are required, and the חומש is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'with the ram of the אשם, and he will be forgiven'. The ram and the payment hold back atonement in הקדש, but the fifth does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the חומש does not block atonement. Forgiveness depends only on the ram and the payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links forgiveness to the ram and the אשם alone. Since the חומש is not mentioned there, it is not required for atonement. He still owes the חומש, but if he has not paid it yet, his atonement is not blocked.

steps.title: הקדש and הדיוט teach each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the laws of הקדש and of a regular person's money (גזל הגר) can be learned from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let הקדש be learned from הדיוט, and הדיוט from הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a two-way comparison between מעילה and גזל הגר. This is a setup line, and the next step explains exactly what each one teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case states something clearly that the other case leaves unclear. Because the two cases match, each can fill in the gap of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular person; here, money owed to a person (גזל הגר)
And let it be learned

phrases.english: And let consecrated property be learned from common property,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the מעילה rules just derived back to the משנה's case of גזל הגר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The laws of הקדש (מעילה) and of הדיוט (גזל הגר) are learned from one another.

steps.title: What each case teaches the other
steps.stepSummary: From הדיוט we learn that 'אשם' in הקדש means the קרן. From הקדש we learn that in הדיוט, too, the חומש does not hold back atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדש from הדיוט: just as 'אשם' there means the principal, 'אשם' here also means the principal. הדיוט from הקדש: just as in הקדש the fifth does not hold back atonement, in הדיוט the fifth also does not hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out both directions of the comparison. Each case gives the other the piece it was missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In גזל הגר, the verse clearly calls the payment 'אשם'. That tells us that 'אשם' in the מעילה verse also means the קרן. In מעילה, the verse showed that the חומש does not block atonement, and that rule now applies to גזל הגר as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal, meaning the basic amount owed
Of there (here, the גזל הגר case)

steps.whatToRemember: In both הקדש and גזל הגר, atonement needs the ram and the קרן, with the payment coming first. The חומש is owed, but it does not hold back atonement.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'אשם' in the מעילה verse means the קרן, as it does in גזל הגר. In גזל הגר, as in מעילה, the חומש does not block atonement.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of הגוזל עצים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the פרק of הגוזל עצים with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הגוזל עצים.
steps.whatsHappening: The learning of this פרק is finished, and this line marks its official end. It is not part of the argument. It is a closing formula said when completing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion just before this ended with the rule that the חומש does not hold back atonement, both for הקדש and for a regular person. With that, the פרק is done. The הדרן line names the פרק by its first words, הגוזל עצים, and expresses that we will come back to learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The formula said when finishing a פרק.
One who steals wood. The opening words of the פרק, used as its name.

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק הגוזל עצים ends with the conclusion that the קרן and the אשם are needed for atonement, but the חומש is not, both in הקדש and in גזל הגר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as part of the legal discussion. It adds no new law. It is only a closing marker for the פרק.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
phrases.notes: This is the usual line said when finishing a פרק, hoping to come back and learn it again.

phrases.english: [the chapter of] "One Who Steals Wood."
